stories.headline: Taylor Frankie Paul's Ex-Husband Tate Asks Court To Unseal Drug Test Results - TMZ
stories.summary: Taylor Frankie Paul’s ex-husband, Tate Paul, filed a motion to unseal drug test results as part of their bitter custody battle, TMZ has learned.
stories.why: Custody battles involving drug tests signal how social media influencers' personal crises are becoming legal precedents—if you follow creator culture, this shows the real stakes behind the Instagram drama.

stories.headline: Perez Hilton has long road to recovery, had struggled with depression before self-harm, sister says - NBC News
stories.summary: Barbara Lavandeira recalled finding her brother in a state of distress on Aug. 4 and said “we remain hopeful” as he recovers.
stories.why: Perez Hilton's mental health crisis is a reckoning for a guy who built an empire on schadenfreude; it's the cultural chickens coming home to roost about whether that business model was ever sustainable.

stories.headline: Big Brother Eviction Recap: Who Was The First To Go After The Toolshed's Implosion? - TVLine
stories.summary: Big Brother 28 houseguests Chuk, Haley, and Barrett all faced eviction on Thursday night — but which player was ultimately sent packing? Read our recap!
stories.why: Big Brother's drama reflects real-time alliance shifts that mirror workplace politics—watching strategic evictions teaches you something about human dynamics under pressure that applies beyond reality TV.

stories.headline: Selena Gomez and her mom accused of fraud over their mental health startup - NBC News
stories.summary: Superstar Selena Gomez and her mother are accused of defrauding investors of their mental health startup, Wondermind, in a federal lawsuit filed Thursday.
stories.why: Selena Gomez's fraud lawsuit exposes how celebrity-backed wellness startups can be smoke-and-mirrors plays for investor cash, a cautionary tale if you're considering putting money into any influencer-branded health venture.

stories.headline: ‘The End Of Oak Street’ Stomping To $38M-$48M WW Opening; U.S. Previews At $2M+ – Thursday PM Box Office - Deadline
stories.summary: The J.J. Abrams-produced The End of Oak Street is looking at $2 million-plus in U.S. previews for an estimated global box office opening of $38M-$48M.
stories.why: A $40M+ opening for a J.J. Abrams film signals Hollywood is betting on tentpole spectacle as the only thing that moves theatrical needles—where your entertainment dollars are actually going matters.

stories.headline: Tyler Duckworth Dies: MTV’s ‘The Challenge’ Alum Was 44 - Deadline
stories.summary: Tyler Duckworth, who first appeared on MTV’s The Real World: Key West and went on to compete on six seasons of The Challenge, winning twice, has died.
stories.why: Tyler Duckworth's death at 44 is a grim reminder that MTV reality TV stars from the 2000s are aging into serious mortality, shifting your relationship to shows you watched in your 20s.

stories.headline: Christy Knowings, ‘All That’ Star, Dies at 46 - The Hollywood Reporter
stories.summary: Her former co-star, Kenan Thompson, wrote in a tribute, "She was a real one and one of the funniest people out here."
stories.why: Christy Knowles' death marks the end of Nickelodeon's '90s comedy legacy and generational memories—if you grew up on that era, this is your childhood gatekeepers actually aging out.

stories.headline: Teamsters Pound Paramount Over WBD Merger Promises & Threats: “Stop Playing Games” - Deadline
stories.summary: Hollywood Teamsters called BS on Paramount Over Warner Bros Merger promises & threats
stories.why: Teamsters union pressure on studio mergers matters because it's labor fighting back against consolidation that affects whether you see original content or just corporate IP recycling.
